customManagers.description: The `audit` job installs cargo-audit at a pinned version, because a supply-chain gate that installs an unpinned tool on every run is a gate a third party can change without a commit here. Pinning it created the other half of the problem — a version nothing watches — so this is the thing that watches it.

packageRules.description: pnpm 11 refuses to resolve lockfile entries younger than its own minimumReleaseAge (1440 min) and CI installs --frozen-lockfile, so a fresh release would break the install. Seven days clears that window sevenfold. Note Renovate cannot read pnpm's setting itself (renovate#41652), so the two are kept in step by hand.
A major gets longer to settle before it is proposed.
One pull request for the frontend.

The package manager that resolves the lockfile should not change in the same commit as the seventeen packages it resolves — reverting one would revert both. Placed after the npm rule on purpose: packageRules apply in array order and the later entry wins, so above it this groupName is silently overridden back to "app dependencies" and the split looks applied while doing nothing. deploy/Dockerfile reads this field rather than restating it, so a pnpm bump is genuinely a one-file edit.
One pull request for the server.

One pull request for the workflows. Left ungrouped these arrive one PR per action and saturate prConcurrentLimit on their own, starving the groups above. upload-artifact and download-artifact also ship their majors on the same day and are a matched pair — grouped so they move in one reviewable change rather than as two PRs that are each wrong without the other.

TypeScript 7 is the Go-native rewrite and ships no stable programmatic API until 7.1. svelte-check 4.x — the only line that exists — declares `typescript: ^5.0.0 || ^6.0.0`, so `pnpm check` breaks outright on 7. The tsconfig itself is already clean for it. Lift this when a svelte-check accepts 7.

The reason this repo runs Renovate rather than Dependabot. SPEC §06 states that every version pin lives in exactly one of .nvmrc, rust-toolchain.toml or the packageManager field, and Dependabot has no manager for any of the three — so the doctrine's own files were the only ones nothing watched. Grouped so a toolchain move arrives as one reviewable change — which has to include deploy/Dockerfile's node and rust images, because tests/release.rs asserts they name the same minor as the pin files. Left to the dockerfile manager alone, Rust 1.98 arrived as two branches (renovate/toolchain-pins and renovate/rust-1.x), each red on its own and green only if merged together. matchDepNames keeps alpine out of it: no pin file ties the base image to anything, so it may move on its own.
